instructions: Ask only unanswered questions after the four-question kickoff in START_HERE.md. Read LIFE_INTERVIEW.md, GIT_STATE_MODEL.md and CAPABILITY_DISCOVERY.md. Ask no more than four related questions at a time, follow applies_when branches, and skip non-applicable questions. Never inherit another deployment's personal state or authority IDs. New-user personal state lives in a private Git deployment repository; public upstream contributions are separately sanitized.

questions.prompt: What should this personal-ops system be called?
Which IANA timezone is authoritative even while you travel?
Does your operational day use a non-midnight boundary because of night work or another schedule?
How often and at which exact local times should briefs arrive, if at all?
Do AM/PM labels fit your sleep schedule, or should a slot have a custom name?
Confirm that travel/device timezone must never silently replace the canonical scheduling timezone.
Personal-state mode stores your life state in Git, so your deployment repository must be private. Do you accept that private-by-default rule while the public LyfeOS upstream remains separate?
Should setup pin and record the exact public LyfeOS release/commit/tree your private deployment descends from?
Which best describes your current pattern: working, retired, studying, caregiving, between jobs, self-employed, mixed, or something else?
What does a normal week actually look like, including sleep, recurring commitments, and flexible periods?

If you are retired or not working, what would be most useful to keep track of: appointments, household/admin, hobbies, travel, family commitments, volunteering, routines, projects, documents, or something else?
questions.applies_when: employment_status includes retired or not working

questions.prompt: Do you regularly coordinate care, rides, appointments, paperwork, or responsibilities for another person?
Do you live alone, with a partner/family/roommates, or across more than one household?
How often do you travel for work, family, hobbies, or vacations?
Which parts of your schedule are fixed and which are flexible enough for opportunistic planning?
Do you regularly work away from home, sleep away for work, rotate worksites, or live/work from a vehicle or field location?
What is your exact job title and what do you actually do?
What is your shift, normal workweek, sleep pattern, and recurring work-travel or overnight pattern?
Which tools, apps, documents, equipment, or systems are part of your work and repeatedly need coordination?
Do you work solo, with a partner/team, or switch between both?
What reliable facts or statements prove you left home for work or returned home?
What names should the home and away contexts use, such as HOME/ROAD, HOME/TRUCK, HOME/FIELD, or your own labels?
What devices, connectivity, storage, space, or equipment are normally available while away?
Which tasks/routines can happen anywhere, only at home, only away, or need different versions?
Does work pay by miles, route, commission, per diem, load, stop, hour, or another unit that should be reconciled?
If terminal or route mileage is used, is the paid value symmetric by pair or directional?
What repeatedly gets forgotten, delayed, misplaced, or done at the last minute?
What decisions do you keep remaking that could use a stable rule or prioritized next action?
What important information is scattered across email, calendar, notes, photos, documents, apps, chats, or memory?
Which goals matter but lose momentum when nobody notices a missed week?
If this system worked well, which three outcomes would save the most time, stress, or forgotten work?
What kinds of reminders help, and what kinds make you ignore the system?
Which recurring choices would benefit from a checklist, rule, comparison, or recommended next action?
How often should the system review whether its routines and rules are still useful?
What hobbies, recreation, creative interests, or long-term personal interests matter to you?
Do hiking, camping, cycling, fishing, hunting, paddling, skiing, or other outdoor activities need planning or preparation?
Do any hobbies repeatedly need packing lists, permits, reservations, equipment, maintenance, consumables, or preparation?
Do you want skill/progression tracking for any hobby, or should it stay intentionally unstructured?
Do you want help collecting vacation ideas, comparing options, building itineraries, booking checklists, or tracking committed trips?
What matters most when planning personal travel: cost, pace, food, outdoors, accessibility, family, driving time, points, lodging style, or something else?
Would calendar, maps, weather, reservation, or document tools materially help your trips?
questions.applies_when: vacation_planning is true or hiking_outdoors is true

questions.prompt: Which travel documents, confirmations, permits, passes, or references are worth organizing?
questions.applies_when: vacation_planning is true or travel_frequency is not none

questions.prompt: Which recurring habits or routines, if any, would benefit from accountability?
For each selected routine, what frequency and preferred days/windows are realistic?
How much time should a normal session take, and does it have separate component blocks?
Can the routine happen at home and away, or should each context have a different version?
What equipment, space, materials, or other resources does the routine require?
What is the minimum viable version on a difficult day so consistency does not become all-or-nothing?
What counts as complete, partial, skipped, or intentionally rescheduled?
When and how should the system check in without becoming annoying?
After a miss, should it reschedule, reduce scope, ask what blocked you, or simply continue next cycle?
What evidence should drive progression or review, such as consistency, duration, sets/reps, load, skill level, distance, elevation, or another measure?
If exercise is selected, which components belong in a session: cardio, strength, mobility/stretching, yoga, hiking, warm-up/cool-down, or something else?
If a fitness/wearable/activity integration is already connected, do you want supported activity metrics used as optional evidence?
Are you currently in school, certification training, professional development, language learning, or another structured learning track?
What institution, program, course, certification, or learning goal is active?
Where do syllabi, assignment lists, deadlines, notes, readings, and course files live?
What is complete, in progress, blocked, or not started right now?
Which exams, assignments, projects, or milestones have verified deadlines?
What weekly study target and session lengths are realistic?
Which study methods work best for you?
What school work can be done at home versus away/on the road, and what must wait for a particular environment?
Which materials need to be downloaded/prepared for weak connectivity?
questions.applies_when: education_active is true and works_away_from_home is true

questions.prompt: When you ask what to do next, should the system prioritize deadlines, prerequisites, weakest subject, short available windows, or another rule?
How often should the system check study progress, and what should happen after a missed session?
Should verified school deadlines or selected study sessions appear on Calendar Projection?
Do you want help with meal planning?
Do you already have recipes or meal plans in accessible chats, files, File Library, Drive, notes, or another connected source that should be imported instead of recreated?
Do you want one searchable canonical recipe library with provenance and tags?
How many people do you normally cook for, and does that vary?
What foods/cuisines do you especially like or dislike?
Which dietary preferences or constraints do you explicitly want the system to honor?
What time/effort level is realistic on normal days versus busy days?
Which cooking equipment materially changes what meals are practical?
Do you want deliberate leftovers, batch cooking, or freezer planning?
Do you want pantry/freezer inventory awareness, and how precise should it be?
How often do you usually shop and should meal plans generate active grocery/shopping intent?
Do you need separate home, work-away, camping, road-trip, or vacation meal options?
Which recurring household, administrative, maintenance, or personal responsibilities are easy to forget?
Would errands benefit from grouping by location, context, person, or next trip?
Which active projects should have milestones and next actions rather than vague backlog items?
Which projects are home-only, away-friendly, device-dependent, or equipment-dependent?
How often should active projects be reviewed so stale items leave daily attention?
Which household members affect shared purchases, calendars, tasks, reimbursements, or responsibility ownership?
Which renewals, registrations, memberships, permits, or paperwork should be tracked?
Do volunteer/community responsibilities need scheduling, documents, or next-action support?
Which appointments, reservations, renewals, or recurring paperwork should be tracked?
Do you want help organizing medical appointment/event dates and reminders, without medical advice or diagnosis inference?
If appointment emails are accessible, do you want approved appointment classes automatically reconciled into your private Git state and optional Calendar event?
Which senders/domains/event classes are allowed to trigger appointment reconciliation?
What should happen when appointment evidence is incomplete, conflicting, or low confidence?
Should verified appointments be projected to Calendar, and which target calendar?
What reminder timing should Calendar use for appointments?
For sensitive appointments, what minimum detail is enough for useful reminders?
Should verified revision/cancellation evidence update the same linked appointment/event automatically?
Do you want searchable receipt/order history from email, files, screenshots, or photos?
Do you want an active shopping/procurement list where fulfilled intents disappear after durable purchase evidence is preserved?
Which vehicles, tools, electronics, appliances, equipment, or other assets need searchable identity, receipts, warranty, or maintenance records?
Should manuals, service documents, datasheets, and references be retained and linked to assets/models/parts?
What facts, procedures, specs, or documents do you repeatedly need to find again?
Should verified purchases automatically create or enrich selected inventory records?
Which documents need durable retention, searchable metadata, or expiration/renewal tracking?
Which bulky originals should remain in Drive/files/provider storage while Git keeps canonical indexes/provenance?
Is spending analysis receipt/email-detected only, or are account-level financial sources connected?
Should expected purchase charges be reconciled against posted account transactions and variances surfaced?
Do purchases ever belong to another person/asset where reimbursement should be tracked separately from merchant refunds?
Should subscriptions, price changes, renewal dates, and trial-conversion risks be tracked?
Which spending/household reports would actually be useful?
Are there budgets, savings targets, debt goals, or spending limits the system should surface when connected financial data supports them?
Which accepted reconciliation results should be retained in private Git versus left only with the finance provider?
Which private Git repository will be your canonical personal state and deployment source?
Which email account supplies selected appointment/order/receipt/admin evidence?
Which calendar should be used for selected projections/reminders?
Do you want Drive/cloud storage for bulky evidence or native documents, while Git remains canonical state?
Are account-level finance connections wanted for selected money modules?
Which fitness/wearable/activity integrations are already connected or useful?
Which existing task apps or automations must be inspected before creating duplicates?
Will Scheduled Tasks be used, and can setup verify canonical TZID/local time, enabled state, timing mode, notifications, duplicate count, and an observed firing?
After initial Git read/write verification, may coherent personal state/config/feature changes commit and push automatically with remote readback?
Should verified behavior changes stop at a branch/PR, or is a bounded merge policy separately authorized?
For features you choose to share, do you agree that public-source/privacy gates must exclude private state, credentials, provider references, message/receipt bodies, and unintended personal data?
Which verified event classes should appear on Calendar Projection: appointments, work travel, deadlines, deliveries, routines, study, bills, maintenance, reservations, or selected tasks?
Which target calendar should each enabled event class use?
How should tentative dates, revisions, completion, and cancellations update projected events?
Should projections ever invite attendees, or remain private unless separately approved?
Which priorities/tiers should tasks and next actions use?
Which items remain visible until explicitly completed?
What must never be repeated after acknowledgement or confirmation?
How should a brief report an unavailable adapter without hiding healthy sections?
What tone, terminology, or filler should briefs/accountability check-ins use or avoid?

sections.title: Git state, retention, safety, and recovery

questions.prompt: Confirm that your private Git deployment repository is the canonical home for mutable tasks, plans, routines, appointments, controls, and accepted reconciliation state.
Does an existing Sheet/database/app contain useful state that should be imported or reconciled into Git rather than kept as a second hidden authority?
Should each coherent user action/reconciliation cycle become a validated Git commit with fast-forward push and remote readback?
Should completed/removed history be retained through immutable events rather than deleted from Git history?
Which data should be excluded even from your private Git repository or stored only at minimum detail?
How long should optional raw evidence, logs, and provider-side archives be retained?
What is the narrowest permission each selected integration needs?
Which deletes, archives, sends, invites, force-pushes, or overwrites require confirmation?
Should a fresh conversation recover the personal system from the private Git repository plus selected provider connections after old chats are deleted?
Which scheduled tasks already exist, including paused duplicates?
After every schedule write, should setup verify the full scheduler evidence chain and keep an incident open until an actual canonical-time firing is observed?
If Git or a required adapter is unavailable, should the affected mutation stop rather than silently using chat memory or a shadow store?
Which provider mutations require snapshot/readback/rollback or compensating action if the corresponding Git state transaction fails?
Which condition watches should stay silent when nothing changed?
How will you judge whether the system is saving time, improving consistency, and catching the right things?
